questions.title: Good-Turing singleton identities and exact missing-mass bias
questions.description: Focused known-result theory evaluation grounded in I. J. Good, The Population Frequencies of Species and the Estimation of Population Parameters, Biometrika 40(3-4) (1953), pages 237-264, DOI 10.1093/biomet/40.3-4.237, with modern occupancy-probability context in Amichai Painsky, Convergence Guarantees for the Good-Turing Estimator, JMLR 23(279) (2022), pages 1-37. Let A be a finite or countably infinite alphabet and let p=(p_x)_{x in A} be an arbitrary probability mass function. For n>=2, draw X_1,...,X_n i.i.d. from p, define N_x^(m)=sum_{j=1}^m 1{X_j=x}, K_{m,r}=sum_x 1{N_x^(m)=r}, and M_m=sum_x p_x 1{N_x^(m)=0}. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive from first principles the exact unconditional expectation of M_n, the exact sample-size-shifted relationship between that expectation and the expected singleton count in a sample of size n+1, and the exact unconditional expectation and bias of the usual same-sample Good-Turing estimator K_{n,1}/n for M_n. Determine the bias sign and the complete equality conditions for n>=2. Also derive the leave-one-out representation of K_{n,1}/n and use exchangeability to reconcile it with the direct occupancy calculation. Justify every interchange over a countable alphabet rather than silently assuming finite support. Keep the indices n-1, n, and n+1 distinct, and explicitly distinguish an equality of expectations from a samplewise identity, conditional unbiasedness, consistency, concentration, or risk control. Do not extend the i.i.d. conclusion to Markov, feature-allocation, or other dependent sampling models. Keep active and rejected calculations visibly distinct and disclose unresolved gaps. This L0 task evaluates mathematical derivation and independent review only. Source replication, Python/R implementation, simulation, Lean formalization, and novelty claims are not applicable.
